newsitem.title: UK: Kenwood advises vote against merger proposal.
newsitem.headline: Kenwood advises vote against merger proposal.

text.p: Kenwood Appliances Plc said on Tuesday it is advising shareholders to vote against an EGM resolution calling for the household appliance group to consider merging with another company.

The resolution, put forward by shareholders representing around 10.4 percent of Kenwood's issued share capital, requires that Kenwood engage in discussions with third parties with a view to soliciting an offer for the Company.
"The board believes that the proposed resolution is damaging to shareholder value and is not in the best interests of the company or its shareholders," said Kenwood in a statement.

The resolution, put forward by the UKAV Continuation Fund Inc., Kalco Investments Ltd, Everest Capital Fund and Everest Capital International Ltd, will be voted on at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on December 16.

Kenwood said the resolution fails to recognise the measures already being taken to strengthen the business and that putting the company up for sale would not maximise shareholder value and would be damaging to the ongoing business.

David Nash, chairman of Kenwood, said, "The board will always consider any serious and credible offers proposed to it without being required to solicit offers from third parties. The resolution is, therefore, unnecessary and counter-productive."
